findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security requirements
findings.evidence: "security":[] on the operation, while it creates a reimbursement and its 401 response implies auth is required.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty security override or set it to oauth2 with reimbursements:write scope, matching sibling operations.

findings.title: Card vault POST returns sensitive PAN/CVV with no documented scope warning
findings.evidence: Summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' returns PCILimit containing card.pan and card.cvv, with no description of data handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description stating the response contains PCI data, must not be logged, and how to handle it; split limit creation from detail retrieval.

findings.title: Physical card GET uses 201 instead of 200
findings.evidence: responses: "201": {"description":"Success"} for a GET, with no 200 response defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for the GET success response.

findings.title: Physical card GET response includes full_card_number unmarked
findings.evidence: CardShipping has "full_card_number":{"type":"string","description":"The full card number."} and is referenced from PhysicalCard fulfillment.shipping, returned by GET physical card endpoints with cards:read scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from the shipping object or move it behind the read_vault scope with a clear sensitivity note.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete'
findings.evidence: Operation is a GET with "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" but it only returns a VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card'.

findings.title: Physical card DELETE uses 'Terminate' but no irreversibility warning in summary
findings.evidence: Description says 'irreversible' but the operation is DELETE with summary 'Terminate a card'; no description of effect on linked funds or 200/204 implications.
findings.suggested_fix: Document in the description what termination affects and that the card cannot be reactivated.

findings.title: Unsuspend and suspend use mismatched operation shapes
findings.evidence: DELETE returns 200 with PhysicalCard and no 400 error; POST has a 400 error response and a description 'The suspension is revertable.'
findings.suggested_fix: Give both operations the same error response set and document the reversal behavior on the DELETE.

findings.title: Pagination parameters inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use 'start' as a cursor on the last entity ID; transactions add include_count; physical cards list has no page_size or start parameters at all, though it returns PaginatedResponse with next.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same start and page_size parameters to physical cards and document one cursor contract across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Pagination 'start' cursor described ambiguously
findings.evidence: Description: "The ID of the last entity of the previous page" with schema type string and no format, while page.next is a full URL.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the cursor is opaque, and that clients should follow page.next instead of constructing start values manually.

findings.title: Page size documented as minimum 2 without schema bounds
findings.evidence: Description says 'must be between 2 and 100' but schema is {"default":20,"type":"integer"} with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2 and maximum: 100 to the schema.

findings.title: Inconsistent user filter naming across endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is named 'userId' (camelCase) while every other filter uses snake_case, e.g. user_id on physical cards and transactions.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id and keep userId only as a deprecated alias for a transition period.

findings.title: Camel-case sort parameter among snake_case ones
findings.evidence: Parameter 'orderByAmountAsc' sits beside order_by_amount_desc and order_by_date_asc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to order_by_amount_asc.

findings.title: Transactions tag duplicates existing tag with different casing
findings.evidence: Top-level tags include {"name":"transactions"} with no description, while PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id} lists tags ["Transaction","transactions"].
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the lowercase tag and use 'Transaction' consistently.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload uses 'reimbursement/' path
findings.evidence: Path uses singular 'reimbursement' while all other reimbursement paths use 'reimbursements' (e.g. /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/receipts or similar plural form.

findings.title: Receipt upload idempotency key in body and header conflicts
findings.evidence: Receipt upload requires idempotency_key in the multipart body, while card vault uses an optional X-Idempotency-Key header; no other POST documents idempotency.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header) consistently and document retry and duplicate behavior for each create endpoint.

findings.title: Physical card create and vault create have no idempotency on card creation
findings.evidence: Create operation has no idempotency parameter, unlike POST /developer/v1/cards/vault which has X-Idempotency-Key.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an optional idempotency key header to physical card creation with documented retry semantics.

findings.title: Physical card POST error body is untyped string
findings.evidence: 400 response content schema is {"type":"string"} while every other 400 uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Return DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 response.

findings.title: Many operations missing documented error responses
findings.evidence: These operations declare only 200 (plus no 400/401/404), while the same API documents 400 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse elsewhere; 404 for unknown card or reimbursement IDs is never documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 400, 401, 404 responses with DeveloperApiErrorResponse for every operation that takes an ID or input.

findings.title: Error responses lack documented 404 and 401 on card and transaction reads
findings.evidence: Only 400 'raises CardInvalidInput' or 'raises TransactionInvalidInput' is documented; an unknown ID or missing scope has no documented response.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 401, 403, and 404 responses referencing DeveloperApiErrorResponse.

findings.title: Error description text is inconsistent and internal
findings.location: 400 responses on card and transaction endpoints
findings.evidence: Descriptions read 'raises CardInvalidInput' and 'raises TransactionInvalidInput', exposing internal exception names rather than what the client should do.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a plain description such as 'Invalid request parameters' and document error_code values.

findings.title: Transaction amount field typed inconsistently
findings.evidence: In Transaction, amount is type number; in SingleTransaction, same field is type string, both marked deprecated.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same type for amount in both schemas, or remove the deprecated field.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'spend_limit_id' and 'fund_id' duplicate each other
findings.evidence: spend_limit_id is deprecated and described as 'Alias of fund_id', and the request body uses spend_allocation_id for the same concept in ApiMileageReimbursementCreateRequestBody.
findings.suggested_fix: Unify the request field name with fund_id and document the replacement in the deprecation note.

findings.title: Mileage create uses spend_allocation_id, responses use fund_id
findings.evidence: Request field spend_allocation_id, whereas the response Reimbursement exposes fund_id and deprecated spend_limit_id, with no mention of spend_allocation.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the request field to fund_id to match the response.

findings.title: Physical card create body uses fund_id yet docs mention auto_routing_enabled
findings.evidence: fund_id description says 'auto_routing_enabled cannot be passed in', but the field is named automatic_routing_enabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the description to refer to automatic_routing_enabled.

findings.title: Card vault spend restrictions use different limit field semantics
findings.evidence: Example sets allowed_categories to [18,20] and limit amount 500000 but the request schema allows spending_restrictions without limit documentation, while the response restriction 'limit' is readOnly and nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the units and whether the limit is required, and align read and write models.

findings.title: Transaction merchant_category_code described as required-by-type but nullable in example
findings.evidence: merchant_category_code is type string without nullable, but the example and the Transaction example show null.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark merchant_category_code as nullable.

findings.title: Accounting category type enum differs from field selection enum
findings.evidence: Enum includes SALES_TAX_CODE description, but the transaction example uses type 'Subsidiary' and reimbursement example uses 'Subsidiary' in accounting field type, which is not in the enum.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the example values match the enum exactly, e.g. SUBSIDIARY.

findings.title: Transaction accounting_field_selections type values conflict with enum
findings.evidence: Example contains "type":"Subsidiary" in accounting_field_selections while the schema enum is uppercase SUBSIDIARY.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct example values to use the documented uppercase enum.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'amount' removed; sync fields unclear
findings.evidence: Reimbursement lists sync_status readOnly but has no enum default and filter sync_status supersedes sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits, which are still documented as active.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits as deprecated in the filter docs.

findings.title: Transaction filter 'updated_after' referenced but absent from list parameters
findings.evidence: updated_at description says it is 'used by the updated_after filter', but GET /developer/v1/transactions defines no updated_after parameter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the updated_after query parameter to the transactions list or correct the description.

findings.title: Transactions PATCH uses destructive flag without warning on replace
findings.evidence: Description says send line_items to 'create or replace' the split and an empty array to unsplit, with x-destructive true but no note on losing existing memos or codings.
findings.suggested_fix: Document exactly what existing line item data is lost on replace or unsplit.

findings.title: Transactions PATCH sets nullable line_items but omitting is ambiguous
findings.evidence: line_items is nullable and described as 'Omit to leave splits unchanged', while null is not described and an empty array means unsplit.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove nullable or define explicitly what null means.

findings.title: Currency amount fields inconsistent between request and response
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmount uses 'amount' with currency_code, ApiSignedAmount uses 'currency' and 'value', and mileage distance is a number or decimal string.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize monetary object shape and naming across the API.

findings.title: Min amount filters allow ambiguous typed values
findings.evidence: Schema uses oneOf of decimal string or number, with description 'larger amount that the given amount' despite being inclusive/exclusive unspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one type (decimal string) and state whether bounds are inclusive.

findings.title: Transaction filter documentation mismatches 'Data.' text
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date description is just 'Data.' and include_merchant_data on the single transaction GET is described as 'Data.'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write real descriptions for these parameters.

findings.title: Single transaction GET lacks documented 404 response
findings.evidence: Responses only define 200 and 400, with no 404 for an unknown transaction ID.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 404 response referencing DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
